bull.b: TTM revenue growth of 21.7% indicates improving commercial traction and a larger base for future operating leverage. If sustained, this expansion can support scale in the robotics business and provide more opportunity to absorb fixed costs, although profitability remains unproven.

Debt-to-equity of about 0.02 and only 89k of total debt indicate limited balance-sheet leverage. This reduces interest and refinancing pressure and preserves flexibility to fund operations or strategic initiatives, even though the company currently consumes cash.

Appointing a CFO with more than two decades of finance and capital-markets experience adds relevant leadership capacity as Duke pursues growth and scales platforms. Transition support from the outgoing CFO may also help preserve financial continuity during expansion.

bear.b: Severe TTM losses, including a net margin near -611% and EBIT of -2.76M, show that revenue growth has not translated into an economically sustainable model. Continued operating losses could consume capital and make future scaling dependent on additional funding.

Operating cash flow of -1.86M and free cash flow of -1.94M, both worse than 2025, demonstrate substantial ongoing cash burn. Persistent negative cash generation limits self-funded growth and increases exposure to the availability and terms of external capital.

Canceling the 2026 shareholder meeting and withdrawing all proposals pauses formal shareholder decision-making. The absence of a replacement meeting schedule creates governance uncertainty and may delay clarity on the company’s corporate agenda and accountability mechanisms.
